rv.q: "The resplendent Sutton Foster often movingly suggests the dark side to Charity’s perpetual sunniness…The material doesn’t hold up especially well. The sexual politics are obviously dated and so is Simon’s awkward vernacular…The plot is noodly and digressive, but then again that mirrors the heroine and it’s part of her charm.

The New Group’s “Sweet Charity” is a bittersweet, but sublime revival that begins with Foster—in a blonde wig likely to be the only controversial element of this production—being robbed and pushed into a fountain.
